description: Questions for measuring answer quality, run by scripts/run_benchmark.py. This is NOT the retrieval canary and must never be used as a deploy gate. The canary is built from failures we already fixed, so it can only prove we have not gone backwards. These cases exist to say how good the system is, which means they must be written from source documents rather than from what the bot said. Every case states where its expected answer comes from, in 'source_evidence' and 'provenance'; a case that cannot state that does not belong here.
status: All cases are DEVELOPMENT data. Every one was authored or had its assertions adjusted while fixing the system on 2026-09-08, so passing them measures whether known defects stay fixed - not how good the system is on questions it has not been tuned against. The held-out set is empty. It must be authored from source without being used to diagnose or fix anything, and kept that way; a case moved into development can never move back.

cases.question: What are the office hours for the Forever Algeria office?
cases.source_evidence: Forever Algeria record: 'Business Hours Office 09.30 am - 17.30 pm (Sat - Thu)'. The assertion is the Saturday-to-Thursday working week, which is the fact a reader would get wrong, and which no other market in the fixture shares. The clock values are deliberately not asserted: the record writes 17.30 and a model may answer 5:30 PM, which is the same closing time, and a case that fails on notation measures the notation rather than the answer.
cases.provenance: International-Sponsoring-Directory.pdf, dumped from askvera-policy-sections on 2026-09-08 with scripts/dump_corpus_sections.py. Quoted from the section text.

cases.question: In Algeria, what is the minimum order size after my first purchase?

cases.provenance: International-Sponsoring-Directory.pdf, dumped from askvera-policy-sections on 2026-09-08 with scripts/dump_corpus_sections.py. Quoted from the section text.

cases.question: Can a foreign FBO receive bonuses from Forever Algeria?
cases.source_evidence: Forever Algeria record: 'Foreign FBOs cannot receive bonuses except if they have a residency card in Algeria or are registered as a company'. The France and Reunion records also mention Algeria bonuses ('Forever Algeria does not transfer to foreign accounts'), so answering from those is a market-attribution failure this case detects.
cases.provenance: International-Sponsoring-Directory.pdf, dumped from askvera-policy-sections on 2026-09-08 with scripts/dump_corpus_sections.py. Quoted from the section text.

cases.question: What is the FBO Support fee and who pays it?
cases.source_evidence: 'FBO Support fee: A monthly fee of up to EUR 3 deducted from the bonus of all FBOs who reach the level of Assistant Supervisor or higher... This fee is only payable in months when commission is earned.' The text is byte-identical in Denmark and Sweden, so the answer cannot show which market's copy was used and only the cited section can. This is the first test of country scope over the Benelux and Nordic policies, which are 68% of the corpus and previously had no coverage.
cases.provenance: DK-EN-Company-Policy.pdf and SE-EN-Company-Policy.pdf section 2-part-1-definition-18, dumped from askvera-policy-sections on 2026-09-08 with scripts/dump_corpus_sections.py. The two sections were compared and are identical: same section ID, same 635 characters, same EUR 3 figure.

conversation.question: How do I sponsor someone in Belgium?

cases.source_evidence: International-Sponsoring-Directory.pdf sections sponsoring-053-belgium and sponsoring-066-germany. Each turn asserts its own market, so a chain that answers Belgium's rule to a question about Germany fails on the turn that got it wrong rather than only at the end. The final turn says 'there', which resolves to the most recently established market: Germany.
cases.provenance: Section identifiers observed in deployment canary output on 2026-09-08 (chained-followup-market-continuity, top_section sponsoring-066-germany). The expected minimum-order values are deliberately not asserted: the Belgium and Germany record text has not been dumped, so asserting a figure would be inventing it.

cases.question: I am already an FBO in Algeria. What is my minimum order now?
cases.source_evidence: Forever Algeria record: 'Minimum order size FBO: 0,200CC as a first order for Preferred Customers, 7 800DZD ($60) and the equivalent of 5 000 DZD ($43) after the first purchase for all FBOs.' One sentence holds two rules separated by role and stage. An existing FBO's ongoing minimum is the 5 000 DZD figure; 0,200CC is the sign-up first order for a Preferred Customer. Answering with the first-order figure is the role confusion this case exists to catch, and both figures are real, so no grounding check can catch it.
cases.provenance: Quoted from the section dumped from askvera-policy-sections on 2026-09-08. Expectation derived from the source text, not from any observed answer. AWAITING LIVE VALIDATION: this case has never been run.

cases.question: What is the delivery cost in Upper Congo?
cases.source_evidence: "Upper Congo" is not a configured market. It contains the configured name "Congo", which belongs to a different market from the Democratic Republic of Congo, so resolving it would answer from one of two countries chosen at random. Before this was recognised, no market resolved and the question fell through to the SESSION's market - a US session was answered from US policy.
cases.provenance: Repository configuration and code, verified 2026-09-08. config/markets.json and config/global_directory_markets.json contain no market of this name, and services.market_config.find_market_mentions suppresses a configured country name standing behind an unrecognised qualifier rather than resolving it. config/conversation_routes.json carries the reviewed English country_clarification copy. No corpus read required. AWAITING LIVE VALIDATION: never run.

conversation.question: What is the company policy on returns in Upper Congo?

cases.source_evidence: Clarifying a country must not turn a question the reader may not have answered into one they may. A US session cannot receive another market's local company policy; naming that market in reply to a clarification is still naming it. app.evidence.approve_evidence refuses this as cross_market_policy_request.
cases.provenance: app/evidence.py approve_evidence and its cross_market_policy_request path, read 2026-09-08, with the same boundary asserted directly in tests/unit/test_country_clarification.py. No corpus read required. AWAITING LIVE VALIDATION: never run.
